audit.whatIsWrong: Ground Slam's attack-speed slow is described only as blunting his autos — "his on-hit autos start bouncing off your armor". The strongest thing it does in this specific matchup is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's text for Spirit Cleave says outright that "Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed". Ground Slam is the only attack-speed slow in your kit and it is on a 7-second cooldown, so every cast directly lengthens the cooldown on Yone's shield and slows the swing itself. Against a champion whose entire sustain in lane is that shield, slowing his attack speed is offence, not defence — and it is the one interaction that explains why the 4-5 window turns.
audit.corrected: Stated in mid, spikes[2], whys[3] and whys[5], with the 14-second base cooldown given so the effect is countable.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (W "Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed", cd 14)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] and mid both instruct you to "hold R until his E spirit is cast out, then knock up the real body where he cannot rewind away" and "R the real body".
audit.why: The kit says only that Yone's spirit leaves his body behind and is forced back when the ability ends. It says nothing about which of the two is targetable, and needsResearch is empty, which means unknown rather than confirmed. I am not willing to ship a targeting instruction I cannot verify, because a player who commits a 130-second ultimate on the wrong assumption loses the fight. The same advice can be given from a number I do have: Soul Unbound is 22 seconds at rank 1 and only reaches 10 at rank 5, so early it is a rare escape you can simply wait out and late it is always available.
audit.corrected: Body-versus-spirit targeting removed; replaced with the 22s-to-10s cooldown and a wait-it-out rule in wants.you[1], mid, spikes[1] and whys[4].
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (E "Yone's spirit leaves his body behind... forced back to his body", cd 22/19/16/13/10; needsResearch all null)

audit.whatIsWrong: No ultimate cooldowns anywhere, and late frames the fed-Yone problem purely as damage: "his Q3 knock-up and crit out-damage your armor".
audit.why: Fate Sealed is 120/100/80 against Unstoppable Force's 130/115/100 — Yone's ultimate is back first at every rank, by 10 seconds early and 20 late. That is the structural reason you cannot play the late game as a trade-ultimates duel, and it is a stronger argument for the entry's own conclusion (peel, don't hunt him) than the damage comparison it currently uses. Way of the Hunter also matters: every second attack deals MAGIC damage, so armour answers only half of his auto profile.
audit.corrected: Ultimate cooldowns added to spikes[3] and whys[6]; the magic-damage half of his passive added to late.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (R 120/100/80; P "deals magic damage with every second Attack")

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Malphite / Skill / Yone / Yone / Malphite / Yone / Yone and disagrees with its own whys at four stages.
audit.why: win[0] says Malphite while whys[0] says "Yone's Q poke and W shield out-trade you" and early says "Yone owns the opening". win[1] says Skill while whys[1] says "still his window". win[2] says Yone while whys[2] says "trades even out". win[5] says Yone while spikes[2] calls the first item "your power peak, force every trade here" and whys[5] calls it "your armor-stacking peak". Levels 4-5 are the only genuinely split stage — whys[3] gives you the armour and gives him the rewind — so that one becomes Skill rather than his.
audit.corrected: Yone / Yone / Skill / Skill / Malphite / Malphite / Yone, which matches every prose field and the 53.94% win rate over 1817 games.
sources: champ-data/content/malphite.js (early, spikes[2], whys[0], whys[1], whys[2], whys[5])

edits.before: Yone owns the opening — his Q poke and W spirit-cleave chip you while you have no trade pattern and just eat damage before W and E come online. Don't walk up to last-hit into his Q; use the tip of your own Q to farm and let Granite Shield refresh between his pokes. Accept that pre-3 is his window and don't trade back yet — your E attack-speed slow and W armor simply aren't online to punish him.
edits.after: Yone owns the opening — Mortal Steel pokes every 4 seconds and Spirit Cleave shields him for it, while you have no trade pattern before Thunderclap and Ground Slam. Don't walk up into his Q; farm with the tip of Seismic Shard and step out so Granite Shield recharges. One thing worth knowing now: his shield is smallest in a 1v1, since Spirit Cleave scales with the number of champions it hits. Accept the chip and don't trade back yet.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stabilize as W's bonus armor and E come online — now his on-hit autos start bouncing off your armor and your E slows his attack speed mid-trade. Level 6 is your flip: hold Unstoppable Force until he casts his E spirit forward, then R the real body for a knock-up he can't rewind out of. Bait the R-fake — if he blows E to dodge, your next R is a free all-in.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stabilize, and Ground Slam does more than you think: Spirit Cleave's cooldown scales with attack speed, so slowing him stretches a 14-second shield further while blunting his autos. Level 6 is your flip, and it is a counting job — Soul Unbound is 22 seconds at rank 1, so commit Unstoppable Force inside that window and he has no rewind. Bait the R-fake: if he spends E, the next is free.

edits.before: Your first armor item (Frozen Heart, Plated Steelcaps) plus W and E make you a wall his on-hit kit can't break — this is your peak, so close the lane here. But a fed Yone reclaims the straight 1v1: his Q3 knock-up and crit out-damage your armor, and E-rewind undoes your R commit. Stop solo-hunting him — use R to flank his carries in fights and let your team punish the dive instead.
edits.after: Your first armor item plus Thunderclap and Ground Slam make you a wall — this is your peak, so close the lane here. But armour is only half an answer: Way of the Hunter makes every second attack magic damage, and by two items Fate Sealed is 80 seconds to your 100 while Soul Unbound is down to 10. He simply re-engages more often than you do. Stop solo-hunting him; R for his carries and let your team punish the dive.

notes: I removed the body-versus-spirit targeting instruction rather than correcting it, because I could not verify which unit is targetable during Soul Unbound and the kit's needsResearch block is empty (unknown, not no). If the user knows the answer, the level-6 advice can be sharpened further — the cooldown version I wrote is correct either way, just less specific. QUESTION for the user is recorded separately. Also inherited from the Zac mirror: Malphite's Q and E "grounding" flags and his R "projectile" flag are tooltip-parsing artefacts and I wrote nothing based on any of them — which matters here because a grounding claim would have been an easy and wrong answer to Soul Unbound and Mortal Steel's dash.
